headline: Vol bled out and Asia's chips bounced, but the dollar took the baton: EUR at the 1st percentile of its year, DXY at the 99th, and the risk regime still slipped to -15.
summary: The pressure point moved again. Yesterday the bill passed from credit to rates; today it sits squarely in FX. DXY +0.3% to 102.54 — the 99th percentile of its 52-week range — with EURUSD -0.8% to 1.1137 (0.8 percentile, -5.2% YTD), GBPUSD -1.0%, USDCHF +1.3%, USDCAD +0.8% to 1.4233 and AUDUSD -0.8%. That is a broad DM dollar squeeze, not a euro story. The tell is that Asia FX went the other way: USDKRW -0.5%, USDCNY -0.2% at the 2nd percentile, USDINR -0.3% with a 1-month z of -3.07. The dollar composite at -21 and rates at -33 are why the risk regime deteriorated to -15 even as VIX fell 5.2% to 18.45 and VIX3M eased to 20.64.

Equities got their relief where the damage was worst, offshore. Taiwan +3.6%, Korea +2.6% (after EWY -21.5% on the month), Nikkei +1.3%, Sensex +1.0%, Euro Stoxx +0.6%, DAX +0.7% to the 99th percentile. But US cash closed 10 Nov with SPX -0.4% at 7,520.9 and the generals still broken: NVDA 168.89, -26.3% on the month at the 5th percentile and 17.3% below its 200-day; SOXX -21.4% on the month at z=-2.36; QQQ/SPY at the 16th percentile. The factor damage is now the extreme in the dataset — growth/value z=-3.25 at the 4th percentile, high-beta/low-vol -19.9% on the month at z=-3.09, MTUM z=-3.03 — against a defensive side that is equally 3-sigma stretched: RSP/SPY z=3.75 with acceleration +3.39, MCD z=3.83, HD z=2.84, SPLV z=2.33, KIE at the 97th percentile. Both tails are crowded. That is a positioning unwind with no recession underneath it: claims 189k at the 0th percentile, unemployment 4.1%, JOLTS 7,523 and +4.6%.

Rates are still the engine and the shape is the wrong one. The whole curve backed up into 10 Nov — 3m 4.24, 2y 4.56, 10y 4.88, 10y real 2.66 (19% above its 200-day) — and 2s10s flattened 7bp to 25bp, the 9th percentile of the year, while MOVE jumped 7.5% to 92.4. Bear flattening with bond vol rising and equity vol falling means the duration market is pricing the risk stocks stopped pricing. Meanwhile the inflation composite collapsed to +13 from +26: 10-year breakevens 2.20 at the 6th percentile, 5-year 2.25 after -14bp on the week, gasoline -20.3% on the month, wheat -11.9%, DBC -5.2% on the week. Yet core CPI is turning up at z=0.93 and the index sits at the 100th percentile. Breakevens at the 6th percentile with core CPI accelerating is the mispricing of the week.

Two fractures worth naming. Brazil is no longer a wobble: USDBRL +1.0% to 5.5639 at z=3.33 with acceleration +2.70, EWZ -26.2% on the month with acceleration -3.46, Bovespa -18.0%. Mexico is the mirror image — IPC at the 100th percentile of its year, +8.8% on the month, EWW +7.6%. Second, the AI electron chain is de-rating faster than the chips themselves: GEV -3.9% (-20.6% month), CEG -3.0%, NLR -3.6%, URA -3.5%, ETN -17.3% on the month at z=-2.47, GRID -11.9% at z=-2.18 and 10.5% below its 200-day. Commodities did offer a hand: WTI +1.5% to 87.37 and turning up, Brent +2.1% to 93.38, copper +1.1%, silver +3.4% after a -12.2% month, platinum +1.7%. Crypto finally stopped bleeding (BTC +0.3%, ETH +0.2%, SOL +0.7%) after a week of -8% to -15%.

good.text: Equity vol is deflating: VIX -5.2% to 18.45, VIX3M -1.0% to 20.64, term structure back to 0.943, and the credit & vol composite improved again to -42.
Asia took the chip bounce the US refused: Taiwan +3.6%, Korea +2.6%, Nikkei +1.3%, with TSM +2.0% and AVGO +3.9% the day before and EWT turning up at its 200-day.
Credit held its improvement: HY 3.34 after -8bp, IG 0.91, BBB 1.13, CCC -6bp, HYG/IEF +0.4% and turning up, BKLN at the 97th percentile of its year.
India is the cleanest trend on the board: Sensex +13.8% on the month at z=3.35 with acceleration +3.12, INDA +12.4% at z=2.82, and the rupee up with USDINR z=-3.07.
Cyclical commodities turned up into the dollar rally — WTI +1.5%, Brent +2.1%, copper +1.1%, silver +3.4%, platinum +1.7% — and copper/gold is still 11% above its 200-day.

The macro floor is intact: claims 189k at the 0th percentile, unemployment 4.1%, JOLTS +4.6%, capacity utilisation and industrial production at 52-week highs. This is a discount-rate problem, not a demand one.

bad.text: A dollar wrecking ball: DXY 102.54 at the 99th percentile, EURUSD -0.8% to 1.1137 at the 1st percentile, GBPUSD -1.0%, USDCHF +1.3%, USDCAD +0.8%, AUDUSD -0.8%. Every one of those is risk-negative.

Brazil is a full spiral and it is still accelerating: USDBRL +1.0% to 5.5639 at z=3.33 with acceleration +2.70, EWZ -26.2% on the month with acceleration -3.46. Argentina -16.8% on the month alongside it.
Bear flattening with bond vol rising: 2s10s 25bp at the 9th percentile, 10y 4.88, 10y real 2.66 (19% over its 200-day), MOVE +7.5% to 92.4, mortgages 7.18%.

The momentum unwind is still accelerating, not maturing: growth/value z=-3.25 at the 4th percentile, high-beta/low-vol z=-3.09, MTUM z=-3.03, NVDA at the 5th percentile, MU -29.5% and CAT -26.8% on the month.
The AI power chain is breaking faster than the chips: GEV -3.9% and -20.6% on the month, NLR -3.6%, URA -3.5%, CEG -3.0%, ETN z=-2.47, GRID z=-2.18 and 10.5% below its 200-day.
The safe side is as crowded as the broken side: RSP/SPY z=3.75 with acceleration +3.39, MCD z=3.83, HD z=2.84, XLP z=2.31, SPLV z=2.33, KIE at the 97th percentile. Defensives are a 3-sigma trade now.

trades.name: Mexico over Brazil
trades.line: Long EWW vs short EWZ: Mexico 52wk high, Brazil in a spiral
trades.expr: Long EWW, short EWZ, dollar-neutral 1:1. Overlay: buy 3-month USDBRL calls if you want the FX leg direct.
trades.thesis: LatAm has split into two regimes. Mexico is riding US nearshoring and a stable peso to new highs while Brazil's currency and equity market are in a self-feeding spiral. Both legs are EM-dollar sensitive, so the pair isolates the divergence instead of betting on EM beta.
trades.trigger: USDBRL +1.0% today to 5.5639 at a 1-month z of 3.33 with acceleration still +2.70; EWZ -26.2% on the month with acceleration -3.46. Against that, Mexico's IPC sits at the 100th percentile of its 52-week range, +8.8% on the month, EWW +7.6% with acceleration +1.51 and USDMXN only 6.3% above its 200-day.
trades.stop: USDBRL back under 5.35 with EWZ reclaiming its 200-day (it is 12.9% below), or EWW losing its 200-day. A -7% drawdown on the pair ends it.
trades.target: 12% on the pair over six weeks; EWZ/EWW ratio back to its 2026 lows.

trades.name: Short the euro
trades.line: Short EUR/USD: 1st percentile and Fed cuts priced out
trades.expr: Short EUR/USD spot or 6E futures; or buy 2-month EURUSD 1.10 puts. ETF stand-in: long UUP / short FXE.
trades.thesis: The dollar is being bid on a US front-end that will not cut. 3-month bills at 4.24 (+35bp in 3 months), 2y 4.56, fed funds effective 3.88 and drifting up — the carry gap keeps widening while Europe's growth beta to a strong dollar is negative.
trades.trigger: EURUSD -0.8% today to 1.1137, the 0.8 percentile of its 52-week range and -3.5% over three months; DXY 102.54 at the 99th percentile; GBP -1.0% and CHF -1.3% versus the dollar on the same session confirm this is dollar strength, not an isolated euro problem.
trades.stop: EURUSD back above 1.1300 or DXY losing 101.5 — that would mean the front-end repriced toward cuts.

trades.name: Fade the duration rally
trades.line: Short TLT: breakevens at 6th pct while core CPI turns up
trades.expr: Short TLT outright, or buy TLT Jan puts ~5% OTM. Futures stand-in: short ZB/ZN.
trades.thesis: The bond market has priced a disinflation that the data is not delivering. Ten-year breakevens at 2.20 sit in the 6th percentile of the year while core CPI is turning up at z=0.93 and sits at the 100th percentile; core PCE 3.12 and rising. Add bear flattening and a term premium that will not die at the long end.
trades.trigger: TLT -1.3% with 2s10s flattening 7bp to 25bp (9th percentile), 10y real +3bp to 2.66 and 19% above its 200-day, 30y pinned at 5.26, and MOVE +7.5% to 92.4 — bond vol rising while VIX falls 5.2%.
trades.stop: 10y below 4.70 / TLT above 84, which would signal a genuine growth scare rather than a term-premium problem.

trades.name: Electrons de-rate, regulated cashflows don't
trades.line: Short GRID vs long XLU: the AI power trade keeps breaking
trades.expr: Short GRID (or an equal-weight GEV/ETN/VST basket), long XLU, 1:1 dollars.
trades.thesis: The AI capex chain is unwinding from the power end, where multiples were most extreme. Equipment and merchant generation carry the capex risk; regulated utilities carry the rate-base. As the discount rate stays high, the market is paying for the latter and dumping the former.
trades.trigger: Another session of forced selling in the complex: GEV -3.9% (-20.6% on the month, z=-2.03), NLR -3.6%, URA -3.5%, CEG -3.0%, VST -2.0%. GRID is -11.9% on the month at z=-2.18 and 10.5% below its 200-day with relative strength -8.5%; ETN z=-2.47 with relative strength -14.1%. XLU is +5.6% on the month with acceleration +1.14.
trades.stop: GRID reclaims its 200-day or SMH turns back up through its 50-day — that would mean the whole AI complex is bottoming together. -8% on the pair.
trades.target: 12% on the pair; GRID/XLU ratio back to its summer lows.

trades.name: Energy off the washout
trades.line: Long XLE: Brent +2.1%, WTI turning up off a -6.8% month
trades.expr: Long XLE; add XOP for beta. Options: Jan XLE 62 calls.
trades.thesis: Crude flushed 6.8% in a month and the equities flushed harder, but the majors never broke trend. Energy still has the best three-month relative strength of any cyclical sector while the rest of the commodity complex disinflates.
trades.trigger: WTI +1.5% to 87.37 and turning up, Brent +2.1% to 93.38, both back at their 200-day; XOP +0.8% after -8.4% on the week; XOM and CVX trends up at 6.3% and 9.4% above their 200-days; XLE relative strength +5.3% over three months and in an up state; oil/gold +15.7% over three months.
trades.stop: WTI back below 82 or XLE through 59 — that would confirm the demand read in gasoline (-20.3% on the month) over the crude bounce.

trades.name: India over the EM index
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EEM: Sensex z=3.35, rupee z=-3.07
trades.expr: Long INDA, short EEM, 1:1 dollars. The short leg strips out the dollar and the Korea/Taiwan semis beta.
trades.thesis: EM is not one asset this month. India has a strengthening currency, no semiconductor cycle exposure and a market breaking out of a year-long base; the EM index is 30% North Asian chips plus a Brazilian currency crisis. Own the divergence, not the beta.
trades.trigger: Sensex +1.0% today, +13.8% on the month at z=3.35 with acceleration +3.12; INDA +12.4% on the month at z=2.82 with acceleration +2.86 and relative strength +16.6%. USDINR -3.2% on the month at z=-3.07. EEM is -9.3% on the month at z=-1.96 with EEM/SPY at the 13th percentile, dragged by EWY -21.5% and EWZ -26.2%.
trades.stop: USDINR back above 95, or INDA giving up 6% of relative performance to EEM — the crowding in India is real and a 3-sigma move invites a shakeout.
